payload.claim: The acceptance criterion requires the build command to name "the binary spelled from the selected runtime," but no test in tests/test_preflight.py ever checks that apple's own binary name (`container`) appears in a build line. The witness's apple-dialect assertions (`detail.count("build -t")`, the `-t {tag} -f {dockerfile} .` substrings, `detail.count(str(root))`) never pin the prefix before `build -t`, and the one assertion that does check a literal binary prefix (`f"podman build -t {base_tag} " in detail`) runs under podman, whose binary happens to equal a plausible hardcoded fallback. Replacing `binary = runtime.dialect().binary` with a hardcoded `binary = "podman"` leaves every existing assertion in test_readiness_refuses_a_store_missing_the_proxy_or_the_base_and_names_each_build passing unchanged, including the apple-dialect cases, so the suite cannot currently distinguish a build command that correctly names the selected runtime's binary from one that always names podman's.
